Sun damage ate my chest alive. This fixed it.

I didn't notice it happening. That's the thing nobody tells you. It doesn't happen dramatically. It happens in the background while you're living your life, and then one day you look down and the skin on your chest looks like it belongs to someone you don't recognise.

The dark spots first. Then the redness that never fully went away. Then the texture, this rough uneven surface across my décolletage that no amount of moisturiser made any difference to. And underneath all of it, this general look of damage. Like skin that had been through something and couldn't fully recover. Because that's exactly what it was.

Twenty years of necklines and sundresses and vacations and not once did I apply anything to my chest that was actually designed to treat what the sun was doing to it. My face had a whole routine. My chest got whatever was left on my hands after moisturising my face. Which most days was nothing.

UV doesn't stay where it lands. It penetrates into the dermis and breaks down collagen and elastin at the cellular level. Every summer adds to it. The skin tries to compensate, overproduces melanin in patches, loses its ability to repair the structural damage, and eventually just starts showing everything it has been quietly dealing with. The spots. The redness. The texture. The crepe. That's not aging. That's a bill for thirty summers of unprotected skin.

I tried a few things. Nothing touched it. I was starting to think the damage was just permanent.

Then I found Besque Magic Body Oil. Seven cold pressed oils, made in England, nothing synthetic. The rosehip contains trans-retinoic acid, a natural retinoid that drives cell turnover in the dermis. The vitamin E works directly on oxidative damage from UV exposure. The evening primrose rebuilds the elasticity that years of sun broke down. Cold pressed oils absorb past the epidermis entirely. They reach the dermis. That is where the damage was. That is where nothing else had gotten to.

Two pumps every morning after my shower, massaged into my chest and neck. By week three the redness had calmed noticeably. By week six the texture had changed. By week eight I looked at the left side of this image and looked at my chest in the mirror and they were not the same skin anymore.

This is a real before and after. This is eight weeks of one product. Besque Magic Body Oil from besque.co

I started noticing my neck sag before my face.

And whenever I looked in the mirror, that was always the first thing I saw.

I am 54 years old, I have been obsessed with skincare for over a decade, and I have spent more money than I care to admit on serums, retinols, and facial treatments trying to keep my skin looking its best.

After I started getting compliments on my face but couldn't stop fixating on my neck every single time I looked in a mirror, I finally started researching what was actually going on.

Turns out everything I had been doing for my face was working. But my neck had been completely neglected for years without me even realizing it.

My skin there is thinner, loses elasticity faster, and because I had been stopping my entire routine right at my jawline every single night, the contrast was making me feel far older than I actually was.

So after trying every firming cream I could find and getting absolutely nowhere, I came across Besque Magic Body Oil and decided to give it a proper try.

I applied it every morning on damp skin after my shower, massaging it into my neck and chest. It absorbed immediately. My skin felt different almost straight away. The texture started visibly changing within weeks.

My confidence came back and I started wearing the necklines I had been avoiding for years. When the women around me noticed the difference they wanted to know exactly what I was using. So I told them. And it worked for them too.

Obviously no single product works the same for everyone but I was genuinely amazed, and it even worked for women who, like me, had already tried everything else on the market.

If you have been pouring everything into your face and completely forgetting your neck the way I did, it is not too late. Get yours now for up to 35% off.

Dealing with meno skin blemishes, dark spots and uneven texture on your chest, arms and back?

You're not alone. And it's not teenage acne. After menopause, hormonal changes leave body skin struggling to regulate itself. Blemishes appear where they never used to. Dark spots linger. Texture feels rough and congested even when skin feels dry.

Most products were never made for this. Besque Magic Body Oil was.

Cold-pressed botanical oils that penetrate deeply, calm inflammation, support skin tone and help fade minor discolorations. Applied daily to the areas meno skin affects most. Chest, arms, back, décolletage.

Real women are seeing visibly clearer, more even and smoother skin within 56 days.

One of the biggest reasons small budgets fail on Meta isn't targeting — it's the creatives, because testing properly requires variations and variations cost money. A single UGC video from a creator: hundreds if not thousands of dollars. An agency to consistently produce and test new creatives: thousands if not tens of thousands of dollars per month. And that's before you even know if the ads convert.

If you're working with a small budget, that math just doesn't work. Holo flips that part of the equation. You just paste in only your website URL and it analyzes your brand voice, positioning, and visuals, then generates ready-to-publish ads, social posts, and email campaigns. But what makes this powerful for small budgets is the variations. Instead of giving you one creative, it can generate batches of different hooks, angles, formats, and layouts in seconds. You can tweak the size, swap visuals, adjust colors, change the messaging, translate it into another language, or even turn a static image into a video without starting from scratch each time. No prompts, no Canva marathons, no waiting weeks on freelancers.

And here's why this matters for small budget advertisers: Meta rewards iteration. The people who win aren't always the ones spending the most; they're the ones testing the most. If you can create 10 to 20 creative variations quickly without spending thousands on production, you suddenly have leverage. Instead of spending your budget on creative production, you can spend it on actual ad testing. What used to take hours or cost thousands now takes minutes. For solo founders and small teams, that removes the biggest bottleneck in Facebook ads: producing enough creatives to find a winner. 

If creative costs have been holding you back from testing properly, Holo is definitely worth looking at. There is a link in the description and a discount code if you want to try it.

3 ways small budgets get burned on Meta:

1. Spending $400 on a freelancer for one ad that flops.

This is the most painful one because there's no recovery. The money's gone, the ad failed, and you can't tell if it failed because of the creative, the targeting, the offer, or the timing — because you only have one data point. You spent hundreds of dollars to learn nothing.

2. Spending six hours in Canva for an ad that runs for three days.

Time is money for a solo operator. Six hours of your life — at whatever your hourly rate would be in the business — for an asset that gets fatigued in 72 hours and needs to be replaced. Then you do it again. Then you wonder why you can't scale.

3. Running the same two ads for four months because making new ones hurts too much.

This is the silent killer. The ads aren't failing — they're decaying. CPMs creep up. CTRs creep down. Your audience has seen them. The algorithm de-prioritizes them. You're paying more for less every day, and you don't notice because the bleed is gradual.

Every one of these is a production-cost problem disguised as something else.

Holo eliminates the production cost.

Get on-brand ads in minutes — different hooks, different angles, different formats. No Canva. No freelancers. No waiting.

The dollars you used to spend making ads now go into testing them. 

Which is the only thing that's ever paid you back anyway.
